items.title: Nick Polites Interview, 1963-10-08
items.q: It, uh, did continue, um, using, uh, quite a good trombone player, Frank Traynor, uh, on trombone.

ctx.x: Well, what about that band? Did it continue on the Frank Johnson band?

It, uh, did continue, um, using, uh, quite a good trombone player, Frank Traynor, uh, on trombone. But, um, by this time, um, Frank Johnson's, uh, uh, idea was, uh, changing. He was, uh, under the bad influence, unfortunately, of, uh, Louis Armstrong. He was one of the first, uh, jazzmen we heard in, uh, in the flesh in Australia. Um, he started to, uh, try and play, um, in a more modern style. Um, not modern jazz, but in a mainstream sort of style. Um, which, uh, didn't suit a lot of us. Um, so that, uh, uh, by…
What about Armstrong coming over there? Do you think that he was doing much improvising or the band was doing much improvising?
